\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{ठिकाण} (ṭhikāṇ)}{ठिकाण (ṭhikāṇ)}]{\mr{ठिकाण} (ṭhikāṇ) — a place, a spot}

\label{lesson:MR-C243-thikan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for a fine thread, then the Marathi for a ladder.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{ठिकाण}}
\textbf{\mr{ठिकाण}} — \emph{ṭhikāṇ} — \textquotedblleft{}a place, a spot\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{ठिकाण}} (\emph{ṭhikāṇ}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{*ṭhīkka}, \textquotedblleft{}firm, right\textquotedblright{}, a form CDIAL reconstructs from its descendants (CDIAL 5503). CDIAL lists the Marathi word here only as a possibility; it derives the reconstruction, probably, from Sanskrit \emph{sthita}, \textquotedblleft{}standing\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṭhikāṇ}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Marathi for a fine thread, then the Marathi for a ladder, then say \emph{ṭhikāṇ} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\mr{कढई} (kaḍhaī)}{कढई (kaḍhaī)}]{\mr{कढई} (kaḍhaī) — a wok}

\label{lesson:MR-C243-kadhai}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Marathi for an outing, then the Marathi for a griddle.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \mr{कढई}}
\textbf{\mr{कढई}} — \emph{kaḍhaī} — \textquotedblleft{}a wok\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\mr{कढई}} (\emph{kaḍhaī}) is a tadbhava, a word inherited from Sanskrit and reshaped by sound change. It comes from \emph{kaṭāha}, \textquotedblleft{}boiler, saucepan with handles\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 2638). CDIAL glosses the Marathi word \textquotedblleft{}cauldron for boiling sugarcane juice\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
